newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends lower, capping slow trading day.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends lower, capping slow trading day.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended modestly lower, capping a day of slow trade with pressure linked to reports of a continued weak tone to cash lumber prices, traders said.
Lumber closed $0.30 to $2.00 per thousand board feet lower with May off the least at $389.00 and July off $1.60 at $382.90 per tbf.

Futures drifted on both sides of previous levels early but moved lower around midsession on selling by Refco in July. Prices were weak late as indications for Tuesday again pointed to a weak tone to cash on slow demand, they said.
Outside factors appeared to have little impact on the market, they added.

The U.S. Commerce Department reported completions of new privately-owned housing units down 10.4 percent in March to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.400 million units from 1.563 million units in February.

Opening talks between British Columbia forest companies and unions were cancelled Monday by the companies before they started. The companies want a wildcat strike by loggers ended in the Fraser Valley, northeast of Vancouver, before they start talks on contracts that expire at midnight on June 14.
